exclusions: Shasta-era client branches (the 192-block source limit and parent-anchor calldata decoding) and everything Etna.
Authenticated L1 inputs, parent inputs read from L2, blob field-element decoding and data availability.
The Anchor contract: anchorV4 is trusted to succeed and to record the running maximum of checkpoint block numbers.
Execution, sender filtering, zk gas, base fee, mixHash, the anchor's L1 hash and state root, Engine API and signed anchor encoding.
Bridge verification, proof/bond settlement, consensus security and guaranteed eventual inclusion.
Whole-client equivalence and decoder resource bounds.
drift: Version words below 2^64 with low 32 bits equal to 1 are accepted by the modeled clients.
The size word uses only its low 64 bits, matching Go big.Int.Uint64() and the Rust decoder.
Proposer anchor 0 is validated normally; it does not request inherited metadata.
A proposer source defaults unless one of its blocks raises the anchor above the parent's; the prose names this penalty only where it exempts forced sources.
Forced sources can default when inherited metadata fails validation; no inclusion deadline is proved.
A default block takes the timestamp lower bound without validation and can be later than the proposal timestamp; the proved drift bound covers it.
Zlib/RLP and transaction grammar use explicit checked decoder behavior beyond prose detail.
Extra data keeps the proposal ID's low six bytes; Proposed.id is a uint48, so it always fits as Derivation.md requires.
A nonzero-ID proposal without sources derives no blocks, as in Go, while Rust returns an error; Inbox.propose always appends the proposer's source.
